subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: computeFitScale returns one factor, min(availW/designWidth, availH/designHeight), clamped below by MIN_SCALE. The factor is applied as transform: scale(s) on the fixed-size canvas, so both axes scale together and the internal composition does not reflow. availW and availH come from the viewport minus the same per-mode insets that position the stage-area element. At 1280×720 the scale is about 1.436 in present mode (availW 1264, availH 568) and 1.0 in browse mode (availW 880 with the TOC, availH 464). At 390×844 browse it is about 0.425 (availW 374). Each result fits the stage area, and MIN_SCALE does not take effect at these viewports.

criteria.rationale: Both verify and inspect (repo and bootstrap-template copies, which are identical) start the preview through Vite's preview() API, via startPreview in lib/preview.mjs, which returns a close() that calls server.close(). Both scripts call it from a finally block. That block covers success, a failed check, a Chromium launch failure, and any error after the preview started. It also closes the browser. criteria.rationale: waitForReady polls with a 20s deadline (`timeoutMs = 20000`) and throws on expiry. criteria.rationale: The criterion is met: no browser test uses a fixed sleep, and step waits poll observable state. There are three browser-driving test files: e2e-001-verify, e2e-002-failures and int-002-inspect. int-001-bootstrap also runs `npm run verify` on bootstrapped apps. All four are quoted in full. None of them drives Playwright directly or calls a fixed sleep. Each one awaits a subprocess through run() and asserts only after the child has closed. In tests/helpers/proc.ts, run() uses setTimeout only as a process-group kill timeout, and clears it on 'close'. It never stands in for a wait on state. In e2e-002, setTimeout appears at line 97 only inside an injected-fault source string that runs in the page under test. Inside the scripts these tests run, every step advance is a polling wait on observable state. verify.mjs:96 and inspect-presentation.mjs:77 press ArrowRight and then call page.waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target, with a 4000 ms timeout. A failure throws. After that, verify reads data-step-index again and fails on a mismatch (lines 104-105). inspect checks snapshot.index !== i before it captures (line 84). Judges A and B gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge C says int-002 relies on a fixed settle delay, because inspect calls deps.settle(settleMs), which awaits setTimeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:82; diagnostics.mjs:54-56). That reason does not decide the criterion. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle runs only after the polled waitForFunction on the step index has succeeded, and the index is checked again before capture. The int-002 assertions on runningAnimationsAtCapture read a report written after the subprocess exits; that report is not taken after a sleep that replaces a state wait. The guidance also says fixed settle delays are validator noise, so they neither earn nor lose credit. I therefore rule the verdict of judges A and B: pass.

votes.rationale: Talk.tsx renders the kit's Presentation with steps, title, initialMode and className, and does not reimplement navigation, chrome or the stage. Every step in steps/index.ts uses the single shared Scene, SampleScene. SampleScene is built from kit primitives (SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Frame, Label) and passes `appear` only for newcomers. It writes no motion or layout code of its own. The kit's Stage hosts the Scene, and the kit's Entity supplies layout, layoutId and presence behavior.
evidence: Talk.tsx: <Presentation steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode="browse" className="talk-htm" />, imported from '../../presentation-kit'.
scene.tsx: SampleScene returns <SceneLayer> and maps payload.visible to Box/Arrow/SymbolChip/Emphasis/Frame/Label elements imported from '../../presentation-kit'.
steps/index.ts: STEPS = SPECS.map(...) sets Scene: SampleScene and groupKey on every step, so all nine steps use the same shared Scene boundary.
Entity.tsx: motion.div with layout, layoutId={id} and presenceProps(appear), which every Box/Label/Frame/Emphasis/SymbolChip delegates to.

votes.rationale: Talk.tsx renders the kit's Presentation with the STEPS array, the required title and initialMode, so it doesn't reimplement navigation, chrome or stage. The shared SampleScene in scene.tsx builds every entity from kit primitives (Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Frame, Label inside SceneLayer) and passes the presentation-owned id and the appear flag to each. steps/index.ts types each step as the kit's Step<ScenePayload>. It supplies Scene: SampleScene and a groupKey, so Stage mounts and groups the scene. It has no duplicate motion, layout or navigation code.
evidence: Talk.tsx returns <Presentation steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode="browse" className="talk-htm" />.
scene.tsx imports Arrow, Box, Emphasis, Frame, Label, SceneLayer, SymbolChip and SceneProps from '../../presentation-kit' and renders all entities through them.

votes.rationale: The nine steps are one evolving scene. Every step carries Scene: SampleScene and groupKey 'how-to-make-a-presentation', and Stage keys the scene host with hostKey. All nine steps therefore share one host key, and one scene instance is kept. Each visible list extends the previous one (s2 = [...s1, ...], and so on to s9), so entities accumulate and are never removed. Each entity keeps its presentation-owned id from the E namespace. That id is passed as the id of the kit node and becomes layoutId and data-presentation-entity in Entity. Coordinates are fixed per entity: render() uses constant x/y and slotX. Persisting objects such as you, prompt, skill, talk, tray and card1-4 therefore carry the same identity across all steps. Only the `entering` entities get `appear`, so continuing entities only morph.

votes.rationale: Every entity the sample introduces is rendered through a kit primitive that forwards `appear` to a delayed opacity entry. That delay (0.5s) is at least the continuing layout transition (0.5s) and is applied only to the entry, not to layout motion. Entity applies `layout`, `layoutId`, and `transition={LAYOUT_TRANSITION}`, where LAYOUT_TRANSITION is `{ layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T, ease } }` with LAYOUT_T = 0.5 and no delay. `presenceProps(appear)` sets `initial {opacity:0}` and `animate {opacity:1, transition: appearTransition(offset)}` only when `appear` is set. `appearTransition` returns `delay: ENTER_DELAY + max(0, offset)` with ENTER_DELAY = 0.5, so the delay is at least LAYOUT_T and can only grow. It sits in the animate transition for opacity, so continuing entities' layout motion starts immediately and the newcomer's fade starts when it ends. Box wraps Entity. SymbolChip returns `<Box kind="symbol-chip" {...props} />`. Label, Frame, and Emphasis each return `<Entity ... {...props} />`. All of them forward `appear` to Entity. Arrow calls `presenceProps(appear)` on its motion.svg, so the same delayed opacity applies. Its path `d` morphs use `LAYOUT_TRANSITION.layout` with no delay. In scene.tsx, `render()` gives every entity id in the E registry a primitive with `appear={appear}`: Box (you, prompt, skill, tray, ghost, socket, verify), Arrow (talk, modify, link arrows), SymbolChip (question, link labels, control, pass, modifyLabel, editedFlag), Emphasis (edited), Frame (frame), and Label (reveal). The `appear` value comes from `payload.entering.includes(id)`. `steps/index.ts` computes `entering` as the entities not in the previous step's `visible`, so only newcomers fade in. In `card()` and `link()`, `appear` is also passed to the Box, Arrow, and SymbolChip. No sample entity is rendered through plain markup without entry motion, and Talk.tsx adds no identified entities.

votes.rationale: computeFitScale returns one factor, min(availW/designWidth, availH/designHeight), clamped below by MIN_SCALE. The factor is applied as transform: scale(s) on the fixed-size canvas, so both axes scale together and the internal composition does not reflow. availW and availH come from the viewport minus the same per-mode insets that position the stage-area element. At 1280×720 the scale is about 1.436 in present mode (availW 1264, availH 568) and 1.0 in browse mode (availW 880 with the TOC, availH 464). At 390×844 browse it is about 0.425 (availW 374). Each result fits the stage area, and MIN_SCALE does not take effect at these viewports.

The footer's buttons and progress items are bare `<button>` elements with only data hooks and aria attributes. constants.ts states that the kit carries no visual style.

votes.rationale: The verifier reserves a fresh ephemeral port with freePort() and starts Vite's preview() in-process with strictPort:true. preview() resolves only once this process has bound the port, and rejects if the port is taken, so a stale server on that port cannot be mistaken for ours. The HTTP readiness poll runs only after our own server's successful listen. The failure is surfaced as PhaseFailure('render'). The `finally` block closes both the preview and the browser. This is the fresh-port, strict-port, own-announcement mechanism, with no separate child whose liveness is merely sampled.

result.rationale: The criterion is met: no browser test uses a fixed sleep, and step waits poll observable state. There are three browser-driving test files: e2e-001-verify, e2e-002-failures and int-002-inspect. int-001-bootstrap also runs `npm run verify` on bootstrapped apps. All four are quoted in full. None of them drives Playwright directly or calls a fixed sleep. Each one awaits a subprocess through run() and asserts only after the child has closed. In tests/helpers/proc.ts, run() uses setTimeout only as a process-group kill timeout, and clears it on 'close'. It never stands in for a wait on state. In e2e-002, setTimeout appears at line 97 only inside an injected-fault source string that runs in the page under test. Inside the scripts these tests run, every step advance is a polling wait on observable state. verify.mjs:96 and inspect-presentation.mjs:77 press ArrowRight and then call page.waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target, with a 4000 ms timeout. A failure throws. After that, verify reads data-step-index again and fails on a mismatch (lines 104-105). inspect checks snapshot.index !== i before it captures (line 84). Judges A and B gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge C says int-002 relies on a fixed settle delay, because inspect calls deps.settle(settleMs), which awaits setTimeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:82; diagnostics.mjs:54-56). That reason does not decide the criterion. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle runs only after the polled waitForFunction on the step index has succeeded, and the index is checked again before capture. The int-002 assertions on runningAnimationsAtCapture read a report written after the subprocess exits; that report is not taken after a sleep that replaces a state wait. The guidance also says fixed settle delays are validator noise, so they neither earn nor lose credit. I therefore rule the verdict of judges A and B: pass.

votes.rationale: Tests never hardcode a preview port. They launch verify and inspect with no --port, so the scripts use freePort() (listen on port 0). The 127.0.0.1:4000/5555/1234 values in unit tests are mock origins or injected fetchers, not listeners. Processes are cleaned up in two ways. The scripts close the preview() server and the browser in finally blocks. proc.run() spawns detached and SIGKILLs the whole process group on timeout, so nothing is left behind from a wrapper. The e2e tests also assert the preview port is closed (portIsClosed) and no browser remains (processesMentioning).

scene-kit.rationale: The source supports the pass. Continuing entities move through Entity's `layout`/`layoutId` with `transition={LAYOUT_TRANSITION}`, which is `{ layout: { duration: 0.5, ease } }` and has no delay. A newcomer's visible entry is the opacity fade from `presenceProps(appear)`. That fade has `initial {opacity:0}` and an animate transition delay of `ENTER_DELAY (0.5) + max(0, offset)`, so it is at least `LAYOUT_T` (0.5). `appear` is false or undefined for continuing entities, so they get no delayed animation and their layout motion starts immediately. The delay therefore applies only to the newcomer's entry. In scene.tsx, `render()` gives every id in the E registry a kit primitive (Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Frame, Label) with `appear={appear}`. `card()` and `link()` forward `appear` too. Box, SymbolChip, Label, Frame and Emphasis all wrap Entity, and Arrow calls `presenceProps(appear)` directly. No sample entity with an identity is rendered through plain markup without entry motion. `payload.entering` in steps/index.ts is the visible entities absent from the previous step, so only newcomers fade in. The grouped-scene unit tests also show a newcomer starting at opacity 0 and a continuing entity staying at opacity 1.

scene-kit.rationale: All required keys map to the specified one-step navigation.
evidence: keyAction maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to next, and ArrowLeft and PageUp to prev.
The navigation hook changes the index by exactly +1 or -1, subject to clamping; its focused test exercises every required key.

scene-kit.rationale: Horizontal swipe direction is correctly wired to one-step navigation.
evidence: Touch handlers compare ending and starting clientX; swipeAction maps displacement of at least 50 pixels left to next and right to prev.

scene-kit.rationale: Active navigation entries expose semantic current state and a stable styling hook.

scene-kit.rationale: Focused delivered controls retain their navigation keys without advancing the deck.
evidence: The key handler returns before preventDefault and navigation when the event target or activeElement is interactive.

scene-kit.rationale: Backward navigation is clamped to the first step.
evidence: prev applies clampIndex(index - 1, count), whose lower bound is 0; Footer disables Prev at index 0.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation is clamped to the final step.
evidence: next applies clampIndex(index + 1, count), whose upper bound is count - 1; Footer disables Next at that index.

votes.rationale: The verifier reserves a fresh ephemeral port with freePort() and starts Vite's preview() in-process with strictPort:true. preview() resolves only once this process has bound the port, and rejects if the port is taken, so a stale server on that port cannot be mistaken for ours. The HTTP readiness poll runs only after our own server's successful listen. The failure is surfaced as PhaseFailure('render'). The `finally` block closes both the preview and the browser. This is the fresh-port, strict-port, own-announcement mechanism, with no separate child whose liveness is merely sampled.

votes.rationale: A step that throws or fails to advance fails the render phase with the step index. Absent or non-numeric hooks are not treated as progress. The count is Number(attr), so null gives 0 and a non-number gives NaN, and `!(count > 0)` fails at step 0. Transitions are checked by string equality, waitForFunction(getAttribute === String(n)) and then `actual !== String(i)`. A missing attribute is null and can never equal '0' or any step number, so the verifier cannot step through zero steps and pass. E2E tests cover a throwing step and a stalled transition.

first_results.rationale: The requirement is that when some anchors are present, the skill scaffolds every missing anchor and leaves the existing ones alone. SKILL.md (lines 79-80 and 87-90) says the bootstrap helper does this: only the missing anchors are added and missing dependencies are merged. But the helper does not fully add a missing build anchor. In detectAnchors (scaffold.mjs 89-92), the build anchor counts as present only if pkg.scripts.build is a string. The repo's own test (scaffold.test.ts 73-74) confirms that a package.json without a build script means the build anchor is missing. Now take a partial scaffold where the kit and index are present but the existing package.json has no build script. resolveTarget reuses the root (127-128) and returns missing = ['build'] (137). In bootstrap, the template package.json belongs to the build anchor but is skipped because the file exists (194-197). The helper then calls mergePackageJson with scripts: anchors.includes('kit') (202). Since anchors is ['build'], scripts is false, so only dependencies and devDependencies are merged (161) and the build script is never added. The build anchor is still missing after bootstrap, so the 'scaffolds the missing anchors' clause is not met. The review guidance says to fail when a delivered helper script implements the branch differently from what is required. This is the partial-scaffold branch the criterion names, not an unnamed hypothetical. Judges A and C are right that the helper filters template files by anchorOf, skips existing files, and merges dependencies, so it preserves existing anchors. But that only covers the 'without disturbing' clause. It does not show that every missing anchor gets scaffolded, and the source above shows a missing build anchor that does not. Judge B's reason holds up against the source and decides the criterion.

The bootstrap helper does not fully restore a missing build anchor. - **When the build anchor counts as present:** detectAnchors (scaffold.mjs:89-92) requires `pkg.scripts.build` to be a string. presentation-skill.rationale: The stated contradiction holds. Consider a project where the kit and the index are present, but the existing package.json has no `build` script. `detectAnchors` reports `build` as false, because it requires `typeof pkg.scripts?.build === 'string'`. `resolveTarget` then reuses the root, since `rootAnchors.kit` is true, and returns `missing = ['build']`. In `bootstrap`, the template's package.json counts as a build-anchor file, but it is skipped because the file already exists. The function then calls `mergePackageJson(..., { scripts: anchors.includes('kit') })`. Here `anchors` is `['build']`, so `scripts` is false and only `dependencies` and `devDependencies` are merged. The `build` script is never added, so the build anchor stays missing after bootstrap, and SKILL.md says to run bootstrap and then proceed. The fixture requires that missing anchors are scaffolded. The review guidance says to fail an instruction-governed scaffold criterion when a delivered helper script implements that branch differently. This partial-scaffold case is the scenario the criterion names, not an unnamed hypothetical, and the behaviour follows directly from the cited source.
evidence: `scaffold.mjs` `detectAnchors`: `build` requires `typeof pkg.scripts?.build === 'string'`, plus the required dependencies, a vite config and tsconfig.json.
`scaffold.mjs` `resolveTarget`: if `rootAnchors.kit || rootAnchors.index`, the target is the root and `missing` is computed from that root's anchors, which gives `['build']`.
`scaffold.mjs` `bootstrap`: `if (existsSync(to)) { skipped.push(rel); continue }` means an existing package.json is not copied over.
`scaffold.mjs` `bootstrap`: `mergePackageJson(path.join(target, 'package.json'), { scripts: anchors.includes('kit') })` means scripts are not merged when kit is not in the missing anc…
`scaffold.mjs` `mergePackageJson`: when `scripts` is false, only `dependencies` and `devDependencies` are merged, so `scripts.build` is never added.

SKILL.md says that `bootstrap` copies only the missing anchors, and that if the kit or index already exists, `only the missing anchors are added`. The helper does not deliver the missing build anchor…
